definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She will stay here till he arrives.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle restera ici jusqu'à ce qu'il arrive.

thoughts: The word 'till' as a subordinating conjunction is synonymous with 'until', which means "jusqu'à." It indicates a time limit in a sentence and is quite commonly used as an informal alternative to 'until'.

definitions.note: 'Till' est une forme familière de 'until'.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: We waited till the rain stopped.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nous avons attendu jusqu'à ce que la pluie cesse.

thoughts: "Till" is a less formal synonym for the word "until," and it is commonly used in conversational English. It is mostly used to indicate the time up to the point mentioned. Beginners might find it useful to know such a casual alternative to "until."

definitions.note: "Till" est une forme moins formelle de "until".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I'll wait till you get here.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Je vais attendre jusqu'à ce que tu arrives.

thoughts: "Timber" primarily refers to wood that is prepared for or used in building and carpentry. It's vital to convey this, as well as the possible alternative meanings beginners might come across in common contexts. A note on usage could be included, especially due to its informal use when calling out a falling tree (this meaning is more relevant in native environments). However, focusing on its primary usage related to construction is most practical.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The house was constructed using high-quality timber.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: La maison a été construite en utilisant du bois de qualité supérieure.

thoughts: The noun "time" is very common for beginners and has three main senses that map differently in French: (1) the general, uncountable concept of time (temps), (2) a countable occurrence (fois), and (3) the moment shown on a clock when asking about the hour (heure). These are distinct enough and frequent, so I include three separate definitions, each with a clear example sentence and French translation.

definitions.note: Innombrable : la notion générale du temps qui passe.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Time passes quickly.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le temps passe vite.

definitions.note: Comptable : pour parler d’une occurrence ou d’un nombre de répétitions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: One time, I saw a shooting star.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Une fois, j’ai vu une étoile filante.

definitions.note: Utilisé surtout pour demander ou indiquer l’heure qu’il est.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: What time is it?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Quelle heure est-il ?

thoughts: The word 'times' is the plural form of 'time' when used as a noun. In this context, it refers to multiple occurrences or instances of 'time.' It can also be used to describe historical periods or specific occasions.

definitions.note: Utilisé pour décrire plusieurs occurrences ou instances d'événements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I have been to Paris three times.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Je suis allé à Paris trois fois.

definitions.note: Utilisé pour désigner des périodes de l'histoire ou des moments spécifiques.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The Middle Ages were difficult times.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le Moyen Âge était une période difficile.

thoughts: The word "timetable" is a noun and is commonly used to refer to a schedule or a plan that shows the times at which particular tasks should be carried out. This concept is important for beginners as it is frequently used in educational and travel contexts, like class schedules or train/flight schedules.

definitions.note: Se réfère souvent aux horaires dans un contexte scolaire ou de transport.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I checked the timetable to see when my train leaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: J'ai vérifié l'horaire pour voir quand mon train part.

thoughts: The word "timid" as an adjective describes someone who is shy or lacking in confidence or courage. It is important for beginner learners to understand this common description, as it is a term that frequently appears in both spoken and written English. It is also useful to provide an example sentence that illustrates this adjective in a straightforward context. Additionally, noting its French equivalent helps learners make direct connections between the two languages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She was too timid to speak up in the meeting.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle était trop timide pour prendre la parole lors de la réunion.

thoughts: The word 'timing' is a noun primarily used to refer to the choice, judgment, or control of when an event occurs, or the ability to do something at the most effective or opportune moment. This concept is commonly relevant in both day-to-day situations and specific contexts such as sports or planning. For French learners, translating 'timing' can often be straightforward as 'timing' is also used in French in many contexts, but equivalents like 'calendrier' or 'moment propice' can also be meaningful depending upon the context. I'll provide a definition that reflects the most common usage.

definitions.note: Le mot 'timing' en français est souvent utilisé de la même manière qu'en anglais, surtout dans des contextes sportifs ou de coordination.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Good timing is essential in comedy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Un bon timing est essentiel dans la comédie.

thoughts: The word 'tin' as a noun commonly refers to a metallic element or it can mean a container made of tin. Beginner learners are likely to encounter this word when discussing metals or packaging. Also, French learners might find it interesting that 'tin' is used in everyday context primarily to talk about tin cans.

definitions.note: Se réfère au métal ou à une boîte faite de ce métal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I used a tin of soup for dinner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: J'ai utilisé une boîte d'étain de soupe pour le dîner.

thoughts: In this case, the word is 'tiny', which is an adjective used to describe something very small in size. Beginner learners are likely to encounter this word when talking about objects, animals, or even people that are diminutive. They should understand that it implies smallness in physical dimensions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The kitten was so tiny that it fit in the palm of his hand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le chaton était si petit qu'il tenait dans la paume de sa main.

thoughts: Given the morphological information that 'tip' is a noun, the primary meanings are related to 1) the pointed end of something, 2) a small amount of money given for a service, and 3) a helpful hint or recommendation. These are distinct meanings that beginner learners would find useful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The cat sat at the tip of the branch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le chat s'est assis à la pointe de la branche.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She left a generous tip for the waiter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle a laissé un pourboire généreux au serveur.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He gave me a tip on how to solve the puzzle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Il m'a donné un conseil pour résoudre le puzzle.

thoughts: The word "tips" in noun form can refer to helpful pieces of advice or guidance. Given its common use in everyday language, beginners will likely encounter this word in contexts where suggestions or practical advice are exchanged. It's crucial to convey its meaning clearly with relatable examples.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She gave me some useful tips for the exam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle m'a donné quelques conseils utiles pour l'examen.

thoughts: The word 'tiptoes' is a noun form indicating the part of the feet that one uses to walk quietly or to reach higher by standing slightly on the toes. This is an important concept for beginners as it's a common posture or action people engage in for specific purposes. Translating it for French learners, we focus on the equivalent, which involves the tippy part of the toes or the action of balancing on the tip of the toes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She stood on tiptoes to reach the top shelf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle se tenait sur la pointe des pieds pour atteindre l'étagère du haut.

thoughts: The word 'tire' as a noun refers to the rubber covering of a wheel. This is a common term that beginners might encounter in everyday contexts, such as discussing transportation or vehicles.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I need to change the tire on my bike.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Je dois changer le pneu de mon vélo.

thoughts: The word 'tired' is an adjective and is commonly used to describe a state of fatigue or need for rest. This is particularly relevant for beginner English learners as it is a frequently used word in daily conversations.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I feel tired after a long day at work.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Je me sens fatigué après une longue journée de travail.

thoughts: The word 'tires' as a noun refers to the rubber parts of a vehicle that are in contact with the road. This is the most common meaning, especially relevant to beginners who are likely to encounter it in everyday conversations about cars.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The tires on my car need to be replaced.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Les pneus de ma voiture doivent être remplacés.

thoughts: The word 'tiring' is an adjective that describes something that causes a person to feel tired or exhausted. It's often used when an activity or task demands a lot of energy and leaves someone feeling fatigued. For beginner English learners, understanding how to describe activities that might make them feel tired is useful, as it helps them express their emotions and physical state in English.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The hike up the mountain was very tiring.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: La randonnée jusqu'au sommet de la montagne était très fatigante.

thoughts: This request is to define the noun 'tissue,' which can refer to either a soft, thin piece of paper for cleaning (such as a tissue you would blow your nose with) or a biological material in the bodies of plants and animals. Since this is for a French-speaking beginner, it's important to include both definitions as they're both quite common and would come up in everyday communication.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I need a tissue to blow my nose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: J'ai besoin d'un mouchoir en papier pour me moucher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The scientist examined the tissue under a microscope.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le scientifique a examiné le tissu au microscope.

thoughts:
The word "title" as a noun primarily refers to the name of a book, movie, song, etc.
 or the name or position someone holds, such as a job title or a noble title. These are the most relevant meanings for beginner English learners.

definitions.note: Peut désigner le nom d'un livre, d'un film, d'une chanson, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The title of the book is very intriguing.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le titre du livre est très intriguant.

definitions.note: Peut désigner un terme, un équilibre ou une distinction; par exemple, un titre noble ou professionnel.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She received the title of "Employee of the Month."
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle a reçu le titre de « Employée du mois ».

thoughts: Le mot « to » est extrêmement fréquent et pose souvent problème aux francophones, car il a deux emplois de base très différents : 1) préposition (direction, destinataire, jusqu’à…), 2) marqueur d’infinitif devant un verbe. Les débutants ont absolument besoin de ces deux sens. Pour chaque sens, je donne un exemple simple qui respecte la morphologie (préposition suivie d’un nom ; marqueur suivi d’un verbe à la base form).

definitions.note: Préposition utilisée devant un nom ou un pronom pour indiquer la direction, le destinataire, l’heure, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I am going to the store.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Je vais au magasin.

definitions.note: Placée devant la base verbale ; ne se traduit généralement pas, correspond souvent à l’infinitif français.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She wants to eat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle veut manger.

thoughts: « to » est indiqué comme particule ; pour un débutant, cela renvoie à la particule qui introduit l’infinitif anglais (to eat, to go…). La valeur française est essentiellement une absence de mot ; on peut l’expliquer comme « marque de l’infinitif ». Pas besoin d’autres sens (comme la préposition directionnelle) car ceux-là seraient classés comme préposition, pas particule.

definitions.native: marque de l'infinitif (pas de traduction directe)
definitions.note: S’emploie juste avant la base verbale pour former l’infinitif anglais, comme dans « to eat » (= manger).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I want to sleep.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Je veux dormir.

thoughts: The word 'toast' as a noun commonly refers to two ideas: first, sliced bread that has been browned by heat, and second, a formal call to drink in honor or celebration of someone or something. It's important for beginners to recognize both meanings, as they are quite distinct and used in different contexts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I had toast and eggs for breakfast.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: J'ai pris du pain grillé et des œufs pour le petit-déjeuner.

definitions.note: Cette définition est liée à l'action de porter un verre pour célébrer ou honorer quelqu'un ou quelque chose.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Let's make a toast to the happy couple!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Portons un toast aux jeunes mariés !

thoughts: A toaster is a kitchen appliance used to toast bread. It is a common household item and its translation in French is straightforward. Since its function and usage are universal, a simple example sentence illustrating its purpose will suffice, without the need for any additional notes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I use my toaster every morning for breakfast.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: J'utilise mon grille-pain tous les matins pour le petit-déjeuner.

thoughts: The word 'tobacco' refers to the plant from which cigarettes and other smoking products are made. It's relevant to learn because it's a common substance and understanding its usage is essential for discussing health, habits, and culture. Beginner learners might encounter this word in contexts related to smoking or health discussions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Many people are trying to quit tobacco for health reasons.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: De nombreuses personnes essaient d'arrêter le tabac pour des raisons de santé.

thoughts: Today is typically used as an adverb to refer to the current day or the present time. It is crucial for beginners to understand time references in daily conversations. This word does not have ambiguous meanings, making it straightforward for learners.

definitions.note: Utilisé principalement dans le contexte du temps ou pour parler du présent.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I have a meeting today.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: J'ai une réunion aujourd'hui.

thoughts: "Today" when used as a noun typically refers to the current day. It's important for beginners to understand this usage as it is a common and everyday term. Since its meaning is quite distinct and central, we provide this clear definition.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Today is a beautiful day.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Aujourd'hui est une belle journée.

thoughts: The word "toe" refers to any of the digits at the end of the human foot. This meaning is straightforward and common, making it relevant for beginner learners. It doesn't typically have multiple meanings in English, which simplifies the task of creating a dictionary entry for this term.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She stubbed her toe on the chair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle s'est cognée l'orteil contre la chaise.

thoughts: The word 'toes' is the plural form of 'toe', referring to the digits on the foot. This is a basic anatomical term useful for beginners learning English vocabulary related to the body. Since it's a regular plural form, beginners should easily understand and relate this with its singular form 'toe'.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I stubbed my toes on the table.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Je me suis cogné les orteils contre la table.

thoughts: Tofu is a food product made from soybeans that is popular in vegetarian and vegan diets. It's a common ingredient globally, and beginners in English can often encounter it in various recipes or dietary contexts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I like to add tofu to my stir-fry for extra protein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: J'aime ajouter du tofu à mon sauté pour obtenir plus de protéines.

thoughts: The word "together" primarily has the meaning of being with others or in combination. In French, this can be translated as "ensemble." It is commonly used to indicate that people or items are in the same place or are acting in concert. This would be particularly useful for beginner learners in everyday conversations and contexts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: We worked together to complete the project.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nous avons travaillé ensemble pour terminer le projet.

thoughts:
Toilet in English can refer to either the fixture in the bathroom or the room itself where this fixture is located. Beginners are likely to encounter this word when learning about home or daily routines. The most relevant meaning for them would probably be the fixture itself, as it's frequently used in context.

Considering French equivalents, "toilette" is the usual translation and can refer to both the fixture and the act of grooming or washing. For the fixture itself, "les toilettes" (meaning 'the toilets') or simply "toilettes" in plural form is more common when referring to the room where the toilet is located. Here, we'll focus on these commonly used translations and contexts that are suitable for beginners.

definitions.note: "Les toilettes" est souvent utilisé pour parler de la pièce entière où se trouve le toilet.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I need to go to the toilet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: J'ai besoin d'aller aux toilettes.

thoughts: The word 'toilets' refers to the facilities used for sanitation, typically a room or enclosure containing a toilet seat. It's a plural noun and very common in everyday talk about hygiene and amenities.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The toilets are at the end of the hall.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Les toilettes sont au bout du couloir.

thoughts: The word 'token' functions as a noun and can refer to a variety of concepts. In this context, it's important to identify its most common uses that would be relevant to a beginner English learner. A 'token' can be a physical object that represents something else, like a coin or a voucher ("jeton" or "bon" in French). It can also refer to a symbol or sign (symbol, signe). These meanings are distinct yet straightforward enough for beginner learners.

definitions.note: Un "token" est souvent un objet qu'on utilise pour représenter quelque chose d'autre, par exemple dans un système de transport ou dans un jeu.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I need a token for the subway.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: J'ai besoin d'un jeton pour le métro.

definitions.note: Le mot "token" est aussi utilisé pour désigner un signe ou un symbole qui représente quelque chose d'abstrait.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The handshake was a token of their friendship.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: La poignée de main était un symbole de leur amitié.

thoughts: The word 'told' is the past tense of the verb 'tell'. In French, it corresponds to forms of the verb 'dire', such as 'dit'. The primary meaning to include here is related to communicating something verbally.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She told him about the plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle lui a dit le plan.

thoughts: The word "tolerant" as an adjective generally means being willing to accept feelings, habits, or beliefs that are different from your own. This is fundamental for beginners to understand in both social and cultural contexts, as it promotes harmony and understanding in a diverse world. "Tolerant" can translate to French as "tolérant" for males and "tolérante" for females, which carries the same meaning of being accepting or open-minded.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She is very tolerant of other people's opinions.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle est très tolérante envers les opinions des autres.

thoughts: The word "tolerate" is a verb that means to allow the existence of something, to endure or put up with something, or to be able to withstand something. In French, it translates primarily to "tolérer," and it is commonly used in contexts where acceptance or endurance is required. Beginners should understand this as the ability to accept situations or behaviors that might not be ideal or preferred.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She learned to tolerate his eccentricities.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle a appris à tolérer ses excentricités.

thoughts: The word 'toll' as a noun most commonly refers to a charge for the use of a bridge or road, or it can denote the impact or damage of something, like a disaster. These meanings are quite distinct and relevant to an English learner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: There is a toll on the highway to the city.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Il y a un péage sur l'autoroute vers la ville.

definitions.note: Utilisé souvent pour décrire les effets négatifs d'un événement ou d'une situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The storm took a heavy toll on the community.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: La tempête a eu un impact lourd sur la communauté.

thoughts: The word "tomato" refers to the fleshy, usually red, edible fruit of the plant Solanum lycopersicum, commonly eaten as a vegetable. In French, it is also referred to as "tomate," and it is important to provide a simple example sentence that is relatable for language learners.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I eat a tomato with my salad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Je mange une tomate avec ma salade.

thoughts: The word 'tomatoes' is the plural form of 'tomato', which refers to the popular vegetable (or fruit, technically) commonly used in cooking and salads.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bought some fresh tomatoes from the market.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: J'ai acheté des tomates fraîches au marché.

thoughts: The word "tomcat" is a noun referring to a male cat, often one that has not been neutered. In French, the equivalent is "chat mâle". This term can also sometimes imply a male cat that is prone to wandering or fighting, often in the context of mating. This may be important for learners to understand the full connotation of the word. A beginner English learner might come across this term in contexts related to animals or pets.

definitions.note: Utilisé pour désigner un chat mâle, souvent non castré.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The tomcat prowled the neighborhood at night.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le chat mâle rôdait dans le quartier la nuit.

thoughts: The word 'tomorrow' as an adverb typically means the day after today. Beginners learning English would need simple examples that reinforce this basic understanding.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I will go to the market tomorrow.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: J'irai au marché demain.

thoughts: The word 'tomorrow' is defined simply as "le lendemain" or "demain" in French and is commonly used in everyday language.

definitions.note: "Demain" est plus informel et courant.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I will visit my grandmother tomorrow.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Je rendrai visite à ma grand-mère demain.

thoughts: The word 'ton' as a noun can primarily mean a unit of weight or it can be used colloquially to indicate a large quantity. In context, it usually refers to weight, especially in contexts like logistics, shipping, or other settings where weight measurement is often discussed. Beginners are more likely to encounter it in everyday expressions or in learning about weights.

definitions.note: Utilisé principalement pour désigner une unité de mesure de poids. Un ton représenterait environ 907 kg.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The truck can carry up to five tons of goods.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le camion peut transporter jusqu'à cinq tonnes de marchandises.

definitions.note: Utilisé de manière informelle pour indiquer une grande quantité de quelque chose.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She has tons of homework to do this weekend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle a une tonne de devoirs à faire ce week-end.

thoughts: "Tone" as a noun can have several meanings, but for beginner English learners, the most relevant are those related to sound (quality of voice) and appearance (color or mood). Avoid meanings that are less common or more technical.

definitions.note: Utilisé pour décrire la qualité ou l'attitude d'une voix ou d'un son.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She spoke in a calm tone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle a parlé d'un ton calme.

definitions.note: Relatif à la couleur ou à la nuance d'une couleur.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The room has a warm tone with this new paint.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: La pièce a une teinte chaleureuse avec cette nouvelle peinture.

thoughts: The word 'tongue' as a noun primarily refers to the muscular organ in the mouth, used for tasting, swallowing, and in humans, speaking. In a broader sense, it can also refer to a language or way of speaking. These are distinct but common meanings of 'tongue' that a beginner learner might encounter.

definitions.note: Ceci fait référence à l'organe dans la bouche et à une langue parlée.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She burned her tongue on the hot soup.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle s'est brûlé la langue avec la soupe chaude.

definitions.note: Utilisé pour parler d'une langue ou manière de s'exprimer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He spoke in a harsh tongue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Il parlait d'une manière rude.

thoughts: The word "tonight" is used to refer to the evening or night of the current day. It is commonly used in both spoken and written English to express plans, actions, or events that will occur on the same day, later in the evening. This is relevant to beginner learners as it helps them understand how to talk about plans or events happening in the near future, which is a common topic of discussion.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Are you going to the party tonight?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Vas-tu à la fête ce soir?

thoughts: "Tonight" as a noun refers to the period of night that will occur on the current day. This concept of noun usage is straightforward for beginner learners, and it's important not to confuse it with its use as an adverb. We will provide an example that shows it being talked about as a specific time in an evening schedule.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Are you coming to the party tonight?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Viens-tu à la fête ce soir?

thoughts: "Tons" is a plural noun that refers generally to a large number, amount, or weight. In this context, 'tons' typically suggests 'many' or 'a great deal.' The French equivalent would often be 'tonnes,' especially when referring to weight, but 'beaucoup' or 'des tas' could be used colloquially to describe a large quantity. This word is relevant to beginner learners as it's commonly used in everyday language to express large quantities.

definitions.note: "Tons" peut être utilisé de manière informelle pour dire "beaucoup."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She has tons of shoes in her closet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle a des tonnes de chaussures dans son placard.

thoughts: The adverb "too" has two very common, clearly distinct meanings useful for beginners: (1) "also"/« aussi » and (2) "excessively"/« trop ». Provide one clear example for each meaning and short French notes about typical placement.

definitions.note: Souvent placé en fin de phrase dans ce sens.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I'm coming too.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Je viens aussi.

definitions.note: Placé avant un adjectif ou un adverbe pour exprimer un excès.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: It's too cold to swim today.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Il fait trop froid pour nager aujourd'hui.

thoughts: "took" est le prétérit du verbe "to take". Pour un apprenant débutant, le sens principal — "prendre" — couvre la plupart des usages courants. Les nuances particulières (prendre un bus, du temps, des médicaments, etc.) restent des extensions de ce même sens et ne nécessitent pas d’entrées séparées à ce niveau.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She took the keys and left.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle a pris les clés et est partie.

thoughts: The word 'tool' is a noun used to refer to any device or implement, especially one held in the hand, used to carry out a particular function. This is its primary and most common meaning. The definition will include a simple example sentence that demonstrates this meaning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He used a hammer as a tool to fix the chair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Il a utilisé un marteau comme outil pour réparer la chaise.

thoughts: The word "toolbox" refers to a container used for storing and organizing tools. This is a common item that might be relevant to beginners, as tools and toolboxes are often discussed in simple contexts like household tasks or DIY projects.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He picked up the toolbox and walked to the garage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Il a pris la boîte à outils et est allé au garage.

thoughts: The word 'tools' is the plural form of the noun 'tool'. A tool is any device or implement used to carry out a particular function. Beginner English learners should understand this as a basic word used to describe objects that facilitate tasks. The French translation is straightforward: 'outils'. Here, I'll provide a translation and example for 'tools' in the context that a beginner would likely encounter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He has a workshop full of tools.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Il a un atelier plein d'outils.

thoughts: The word 'tooth' is used to refer to one of the hard, white objects in the mouth that are used for biting and chewing. It's a common word that beginner learners will likely encounter early. The example sentence should be simple and illustrate its common use.

definitions.note: Se dit d'une des parties dures et blanches dans la bouche utilisées pour mâcher.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I have a toothache and need to see the dentist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: J'ai mal aux dents et je dois voir le dentiste.

thoughts: The word 'toothache' refers to pain or discomfort in a tooth. This a straightforward meaning relevant to everyday health situations, making it important for learners encountering medical or dentist-related contexts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I went to the dentist because I had a terrible toothache.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Je suis allé chez le dentiste parce que j'avais un terrible mal de dents.

thoughts: A toothbrush is an essential personal care item used for maintaining oral hygiene. Beginner learners are likely to encounter this word in daily life contexts such as shopping, health, and routine activities. Hence, understanding its basic meaning and application is crucial.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bought a new toothbrush yesterday.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: J'ai acheté une nouvelle brosse à dents hier.

thoughts: Toothpaste is a common noun used to refer to the paste used with a toothbrush to clean teeth. This would be relevant to beginners learning about daily routines, health, and hygiene.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I put some toothpaste on my toothbrush before brushing my teeth.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Je mets du dentifrice sur ma brosse à dents avant de me brosser les dents.

thoughts: The word 'top' as an adjective often implies the highest position or the uppermost part of something. This usage is quite common, especially when describing something that is the best or highest in quality, position, or degree. In French, this can be translated as 'meilleur' when referring to quality or hierarchy. For example, a 'top student' translates to 'meilleur élève'. This is likely to be useful for beginner English learners to understand common expressions related to positions or ranks.

definitions.note: Utilisé pour décrire quelque chose ou quelqu'un d'une qualité supérieure ou en première position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She is the top student in her class.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle est la meilleure élève de sa classe.

thoughts: The noun 'top' has a very common and straightforward meaning that translates well to French. It generally refers to the upper part of something ("haut" or "sommet") or can be used informally to describe excellence ("le meilleur"). Focusing on these meanings will be most beneficial to a beginner learner.

definitions.note: Le sommet désigne la partie la plus élevée ou importante d'un objet ou d'une hiérarchie.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He climbed to the top of the mountain.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Il a grimpé jusqu'au sommet de la montagne.

definitions.note: Utilisé pour désigner quelque chose d'excellent ou de qualité supérieure.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Her pie was voted the top in the competition.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: La tourte de son mari a été élue la meilleure de la compétition.

thoughts: The word 'topic' is a noun referring to a subject that is discussed, written about, or thought about. In French, it is translated as "sujet" or "thème." It is a common word used in both academic and casual contexts. Beginner learners might need to know this for writing essays or discussing specific subjects in class.

definitions.note: Le mot est souvent utilisé pour parler de sujets de discussion ou de sujets d'étude.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The topic of the discussion was climate change.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le sujet de la discussion était le changement climatique.

thoughts: The word "torch" refers to a portable light source, typically one that uses a flame or an electric bulb. In British English, it refers to what Americans call a "flashlight." Beginners learning English need to understand this difference, especially if they are learning British English. I will provide the definition focusing on this light source aspect.

definitions.note: En anglais britannique, "torch" signifie "lampe torche" qui est appelée "flashlight" en anglais américain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I always carry a torch when I go camping.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Je porte toujours une lampe torche quand je vais camper.

thoughts: The word "tore" is the past tense of the verb "tear," which refers to the action of ripping or pulling something apart, typically paper, fabric, or a similar material. This translation and usage are important for beginner learners to understand how to describe actions that have already happened.

definitions.note: Ce mot est le passé de "tear" et signifie que quelque chose a été déchiré ou fendu dans le passé.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She tore the letter in half.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle a déchiré la lettre en deux.

thoughts: "Tormenting" is the present participle of the verb "to torment," meaning to cause severe physical or mental suffering. It is used to describe ongoing or continuous actions of inflicting pain or causing distress. The French equivalent verb is "tourmenter." Since this is a continuous form, beginners might benefit from seeing it used in a sentence to understand its context and conjugation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Watching scary movies at night is tormenting my sleep schedule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Regarder des films d'horreur le soir tourmente mon rythme de sommeil.

thoughts: The word "torn" is the past participle of the verb "tear," which means "déchirer" in French. In this form, it is often used to describe something that has been ripped or damaged. This is a common usage that beginners should be familiar with.

definitions.note: Participe passé du verbe 'tear'. Utilisé pour décrire quelque chose qui a été déchiré ou abîmé.

thoughts:
The word "trained" here is the past tense and past participle form of the verb "train." This refers to having undergone training or having been instructed. The definition primarily revolves around the act of being taught or developing a skill.

In considering what would be informative to a beginner English learner with French as their native language, it is crucial to highlight that "trained" is used to specify that training has already been completed in the past. The French equivalent, "formé" or "entraîné," can vary slightly based on specific context but generally overlaps well in this context.

This is a common word applicable in many contexts where learning or development through systematic instruction is involved, such as in sports, jobs, or other skills.

thoughts: The word "trains" as a noun is the plural form of "train," which refers to multiple instances of a train. The primary French translation for a passenger or freight transport by rail is "trains." Beginners would benefit from understanding this foundational and common transportation-related term. This word can be used in sentences about traveling or commuting. It does not have multiple meanings in this form, so only one definition is needed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The trains are often late in the winter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Les trains sont souvent en retard en hiver.

thoughts: The word 'traitor' refers to a person who betrays a trust or is disloyal. It's important for beginners to understand this in contexts such as betrayal in personal relationships or disloyalty in larger contexts, like politics or war.

definitions.note: Un "traître" est une personne qui trahit la confiance de quelqu'un d'autre ou d'un groupe.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Judas is often seen as the ultimate traitor in Christian teachings.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Judas est souvent considéré comme le traître ultime dans les enseignements chrétiens.

thoughts: The word "trampoline" is a noun and refers to a piece of equipment consisting of a strong, taut fabric stretched over a frame using springs. It is used for jumping and is popular in both recreational and competitive contexts. In French, the word "trampoline" is translated as "trampoline," which makes it straightforward for learners. The definition is simple, focusing on its primary use for jumping, which is the most relevant for beginners.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The children loved playing on the trampoline in the backyard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Les enfants aimaient jouer sur le trampoline dans le jardin.

thoughts: The word 'trans' as an adjective is often used to refer to transgender individuals, shortened from 'transgender.' It's a term widely recognized in discussions related to gender identity and inclusivity. For beginner learners, understanding its usage in context relating to gender identity is important.

definitions.note: Term often used to describe someone who identifies as a different gender than the one they were assigned at birth.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jamie is a trans man and a vocal advocate for LGBTQ+ rights.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Jamie est un homme trans et un défenseur vocal des droits LGBTQ+.

thoughts: The word "transaction" is commonly used in contexts involving business or financial exchanges. For beginners, the focus should be on its typical usage in financial or business contexts, such as buying or selling goods or services. "Transaction" doesn't have any significantly different meanings beyond this general idea, so one definition capturing its primary use is appropriate here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The transaction was completed in just a few minutes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: La transaction a été complétée en quelques minutes seulement.

thoughts: The word "transferred" is the past tense of the verb "transfer", which means to move from one place to another. In French, this is translated as "transféré". The usage is common in contexts where something is physically or metaphorically being moved, like a file, funds, or responsibility.

definitions.note: Utilisé pour parler du mouvement ou transfert d'une chose d'un endroit à un autre.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She transferred the files to her new computer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle a transféré les fichiers sur son nouvel ordinateur.

thoughts: A beginner English learner would likely be interested in the main, everyday meaning of "transformation," which is the process of changing in form, appearance, nature, or character. As this is a noun, an example sentence will help illustrate how it is used in context.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The magician amazed the crowd with his transformation trick.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le magicien a émerveillé la foule avec son tour de transformation.

thoughts: The word 'transformed' is the past participle of the verb 'transform'. It's used to describe something that has changed, typically in a significant or noticeable way. A beginner English learner would benefit from knowing this meaning since it often appears in both spoken and written English. The verb 'transformer' is very similar in French, and the past participle would be 'transformé'. This allows a direct correlation that is easy for French speakers to grasp.

definitions.note: C'est le participe passé du verbe 'transformer'.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The landscape was completely transformed after the storm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le paysage a été complètement transformé après la tempête.

thoughts: The word 'transgender' is an adjective used to describe individuals whose gender identity differs from the sex they were assigned at birth. This is the primary and straightforward meaning of the term.

definitions.note: Se réfère à une personne dont l'identité de genre est différente du sexe qui leur a été assigné à la naissance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She is a transgender woman and advocates for equal rights.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle est une femme transgenre et défend les droits égaux.

thoughts: The word 'translate' as a verb means to express the sense of words or text in another language. It's a fairly common term, especially relevant in contexts involving language learning, communication, or processing multilingual information. In French, it's translated to 'traduire'.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Can you translate this document into French?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pouvez-vous traduire ce document en français?

thoughts: The word 'translated' is the past participle of the verb 'translate'. It indicates that something has been converted from one language to another. This is a common term many language learners will come across. For French speakers, the translation is 'traduit(e)'.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The book was translated into French last year.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le livre a été traduit en français l'année dernière.

thoughts: The word "translates" is the third person singular present tense form of the verb "translate." Its primary meaning involves converting text or speech from one language to another. This is a common and direct verb that has a straightforward usage relevant to beginners learning English.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He translates the text from English to French.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Il traduit le texte de l'anglais au français.

thoughts: The word "translating" is a verb, specifically the present participle form of "translate." It refers to the act of converting text or speech from one language into another. This is a straightforward term for learners as it pertains to language skills and is common in educational contexts. In French, this would typically be translated as "traduire," referring to the act of translation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I am translating a letter from English to French.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Je suis en train de traduire une lettre de l'anglais au français.

thoughts: The word 'translation' as a noun primarily refers to the process of converting text from one language to another.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The translation of the book took several months to complete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: La traduction du livre a pris plusieurs mois à terminer.

thoughts: The word "translations" is the plural form of "translation," which refers to converting words from one language into another. In this entry, we'll focus on this specific meaning as a noun, suitable for beginners learning English. We'll provide a clear example with its translation into French.

definitions.note: Utilisé pour décrire plusieurs rendus d'un texte d'une langue à une autre.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I have several translations of the book "The Little Prince."
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: J'ai plusieurs traductions du livre "Le Petit Prince."

thoughts: The word 'translator' is a noun and it most commonly refers to a person who converts written text from one language to another. This is a straightforward term and particularly relevant for language learners. In French, the word translates directly to "traducteur" for males or "traductrice" for females. This term can also refer more generally to devices that perform translations, but the primary focus here would be on introducing the learner to the role of a human translator.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The translator helped me understand the document.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le traducteur m'a aidé à comprendre le document.

thoughts: "Translator" means someone who translates from one language to another. It's used mainly in contexts where texts, documents, or spoken language need to be converted. This is the noun form referring to people who perform the act of translation.

definitions.note: Utilisé pour désigner les personnes qui traduisent des textes ou discours d'une langue à une autre.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The translators worked all night to meet the deadline.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Les traducteurs ont travaillé toute la nuit pour respecter la date limite.

thoughts: The verb 'transmit' in its past tense 'transmitted' generally refers to the action of sending or passing something from one place to another. This is commonly used in contexts like sending data, radio waves, or diseases. For beginner learners, the primary focus is on the concepts of movement and transfer, which can be easily illustrated with basic examples in both English and French.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The data was transmitted over the internet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Les données ont été transmises via internet.

thoughts: "Transmitted" as an adjective typically describes something that has been passed or conveyed from one place, person, or thing to another. In beginner English, learners might encounter this term in contexts like diseases, signals, or messages being "transmitted."

definitions.note: Utilisé pour décrire quelque chose qui a été envoyé ou passé d'un lieu, d'une personne ou d'une chose à une autre.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The transmitted signal reached the receiver successfully.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le signal transmis a atteint le récepteur avec succès.

thoughts: Le mot 'transparent' est un adjectif utilisé pour décrire quelque chose à travers quoi les objets peuvent être clairement vus. C'est souvent utilisé pour parler de matériaux ou d'une manière d'être honnête et directe. Ces significations sont assez similaires dans de nombreuses utilisations contextuelles.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The glass is transparent, so you can see through it.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le verre est transparent, donc vous pouvez voir à travers.

thoughts: The word 'transportation' as a noun refers to the act or means of moving someone or something from one place to another. This can relate to various modes of transport such as buses, trains, cars, etc.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The city has excellent public transportation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: La ville a un excellent transport public.

thoughts: The word "transported" is the past tense of the verb "transport," which means to carry or move something from one place to another. This is a common usage, and learners might find it useful to understand how to express past actions regarding moving goods or people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The goods were transported by truck across the country.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Les marchandises ont été transportées par camion à travers le pays.

thoughts: The word "trap" as a noun typically refers to a device or strategy used for capturing or tricking someone or something. For beginners, the most common meaning would be a physical device used to capture animals or insects, as well as metaphorical uses like falling into a trap set by someone. Let's provide definitions relevant to learning English as a second language, focusing on these common uses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The hunter set a trap to catch a rabbit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le chasseur a posé un piège pour attraper un lapin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She fell into a trap set by her competitors.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle est tombée dans une embuscade tendue par ses concurrents.

thoughts: The word 'trapped' is the past participle of the verb 'trap'. It can mean to catch someone or something in a situation from which it is difficult to escape. This verb forms the past participle 'trapped' commonly used in various tenses to describe the action of being caught or confined. Given its usage, beginner learners might benefit from a context where it shows a person or animal being caught in a physical trap or metaphorically in a situation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The animal was trapped in the cage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: L'animal était piégé dans la cage.

thoughts: The word 'trapped' is commonly used to describe something or someone that is unable to escape a situation or place. As an adjective, it stems from the verb 'trap' and is used primarily in contexts where the subject is caught or held against their will or intention. In French, this can often be translated to 'coincé' or 'pris au piège'. Beginner learners should be aware of its usage to denote being stuck or caught, often bringing about a sense of urgency or distress.

definitions.note: Utilisé pour décrire une personne ou une chose qui ne peut pas s'échapper d'une situation ou d'un endroit.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The hikers were trapped in the cave overnight.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Les randonneurs étaient coincés dans la grotte pendant la nuit.

thoughts: The word 'trash' as a noun commonly refers to waste material, garbage, or things that are unimportant or of little value. In French, it is commonly translated as 'déchets' or 'ordures'. It is important to provide a simple context to help learners understand the use of this word in everyday situations.

definitions.note: "Trash" est souvent utilisé pour désigner des choses qui sont jetées ou qui n'ont pas de valeur.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Please take out the trash before dinner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Veuillez sortir les ordures avant le dîner.

thoughts: The word 'traumatic' as an adjective describes something that causes trauma or is emotionally distressing. It is often used in the context of events that cause great emotional shock and stress.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The car accident was a traumatic experience for everyone involved.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: L'accident de voiture a été une expérience traumatique pour tous les concernés.

thoughts: The word 'travel' here is defined as a noun. This typically refers to the act of moving or journeying from one place to another, particularly over longer distances or periods. It is important for learners to understand this distinction, as 'travel' can also be a verb, but the current focus is solely on its noun usage. The example sentence and translation should reflect this usage to help users grasp its meaning in context.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Travel can be an enriching experience.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le voyage peut être une expérience enrichissante.

thoughts: Since 'travel' is provided as a verb, a beginner learner would benefit from understanding its basic meaning and usage related to moving from one place to another. An example sentence should illustrate the typical use of the word in the context of a trip or journey. In French, the equivalent verb is 'voyager', which captures this notion of moving or journeying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I love to travel during my vacation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: J'adore voyager pendant mes vacances.

thoughts: The word "traveled" is the past tense and past participle form of the verb "travel." For beginner learners, it is important to focus on this common usage rather than obscure meanings. Including an example of how "traveled" is used in a sentence can be beneficial for understanding its use in context.

definitions.note: Forme passée du verbe "voyager."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: We traveled to France last summer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nous avons voyagé en France l'été dernier.

thoughts: The word 'traveler' refers to someone who is traveling or who travels often. It's a common word for beginners to learn, especially if they are planning to communicate in English-speaking countries as they themselves might be travelers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The traveler took many pictures during her journey.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: La voyageuse a pris beaucoup de photos pendant son voyage.

thoughts: The word "travelers" is a noun and the plural form of "traveler." It refers to people who are traveling or who frequently travel. It can often be relevant to beginner English learners to know how to use plural words when discussing groups, since this can be different from French. In this entry, we'll focus on how to express the idea of travelers in French.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The travelers were tired after their long journey.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Les voyageurs étaient fatigués après leur long voyage.

thoughts: The word 'traveling' as a noun can refer to the act of making a journey or going from one place to another, typically over a long distance. It often implies exploration, adventure, or the experience involved in moving between locations. This is a common noun meaning that most learners would encounter when talking about holidays or trips.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Traveling can expand your horizons and teach you about different cultures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Voyager peut élargir vos horizons et vous apprendre sur différentes cultures.

thoughts: The word 'traveling' is the present participle of the verb 'travel.' This form is often used in continuous tenses or as a noun (gerund). The primary meaning is "to go from one place to another" or "voyager" in French. It is important to provide an example that reflects its frequent use in English.

definitions.note: Utilisé souvent dans des expressions indiquant une action en cours.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I am traveling to France next week.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Je voyage en France la semaine prochaine.

definitions.note: Utilisé comme nom pour indiquer l'action de voyager.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Traveling can be exhausting but rewarding.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Voyager peut être épuisant mais enrichissant.

thoughts: "Travelled" is the past tense of the verb "travel," which means to go from one place to another, often over a long distance. This action is commonly translated into French as "voyagé." For beginner learners, it's useful to provide a simple example sentence to illustrate the past action.

definitions.note: Il s'agit du passé du verbe 'travel', se conjugue en "a voyagé" par exemple.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I travelled to Paris last summer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: J'ai voyagé à Paris l'été dernier.

thoughts: The word 'travelling' is the noun form meaning the activity of going from one place to another, especially over a long distance. Beginner learners might find it useful to know how this term is used to refer to the act of travel rather than the verb form.

definitions.note: Utilisé comme un nom pour décrire l'action de voyager.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Travelling can be a wonderful way to learn about new cultures.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Voyager peut être une merveilleuse façon d'apprendre sur de nouvelles cultures.

thoughts: Given the morphological information, 'travelling' is the present participle of the verb 'travel,' which is used to describe the action of moving from one place to another, often for leisure or work. In French, the equivalent would most commonly be 'voyager.' This form of the verb can be used to describe ongoing actions or continuous activities, such as 'I am travelling.'

definitions.note: La forme continue du verbe pour indiquer une action en cours.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I am travelling to France next week.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Je vais voyager en France la semaine prochaine.

thoughts: The word 'travels' as a noun usually refers to journeys or experiences related to traveling. It's more about the act or process of traveling rather than the specific places or destinations. For beginner learners, the key is to understand it as multiple journeys or experiences consisting of travel. We might explain it contextually using an example sentence that demonstrates its usage as a noun.

definitions.note: Utilisé au pluriel pour désigner plusieurs voyages ou expériences de voyage.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Her travels have taken her to over 20 countries.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ses voyages l'ont menée dans plus de 20 pays.

thoughts:
Le mot 'travels' est la troisième personne du singulier du verbe "to travel" au présent. Cela signifie que l'action de voyager est effectuée par quelqu'un ou quelque chose.

Examinons cela de plus près. En tant que verbe, "travels" est utilisé pour décrire le déplacement d'un endroit à un autre, souvent sur une certaine distance et par divers moyens de transport. Cette action de voyager pourrait se faire pour des raisons de loisir, d'affaires ou autres. Pour les débutants en anglais, il est essentiel de comprendre l'association entre la conjugaison et le sujet grammatical, de sorte que la troisième personne du singulier nécessite souvent l'ajout d'un 's'.

Un exemple pertinent en anglais pourrait être : "He travels to work by train every morning." Cela traduit une action habituelle, souvent quotidienne. En français, cela donnerait : "Il voyage au travail en train chaque matin."

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She travels around the world every year.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle voyage autour du monde chaque année.

thoughts: Treachery refers to betrayal, deceit, or faithlessness and is often used in contexts where trust is broken. This can be in personal relationships, politics, or other situations requiring loyalty. For beginner learners, it's important to understand its negative connotation and association with betrayal.

definitions.note: Utilisé pour décrire un acte de trahison ou une violation de confiance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The knight was punished for his treachery against the king.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le chevalier a été puni pour sa trahison contre le roi.

thoughts: In English, the word 'treasure' as a noun typically refers to a collection of valuable items, often hidden or stored securely. It can also denote something or someone greatly valued or cherished. The primary translation of "treasure" in French is "trésor." This word is relevant and easy for beginner learners of English to understand, especially given the frequent references to 'treasure' in stories or historical contexts. It’s common enough that learners may already be familiar with the concept from literature or films.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The pirates buried their treasure on the island.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Les pirates ont enterré leur trésor sur l'île.

thoughts: The word "treat" as a verb mostly refers to dealing with or taking care of something or someone. It can also mean to consider someone or something in a specific way. Additionally, it is used to indicate paying for someone's entertainment or meal as a gesture. These are the primary meanings relevant to beginners.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: You should treat your guests kindly.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Vous devriez traiter vos invités gentiment.

definitions.note: Utilisé dans le contexte de soins médicaux ou de prendre soin de quelqu'un.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The doctor will treat the patient.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le médecin va soigner le patient.

definitions.note: Utilisé lorsque l'on paie pour quelque chose pour quelqu'un d'autre par gentillesse.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I will treat you to dinner tonight.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Je vais t'offrir le dîner ce soir.

thoughts: The word "treated" is the past participle form of the verb "treat." It is used to describe situations where an action of treatment has already been completed. In French, this would typically translate to "traité" or "soigné," depending on the context. Since the meaning of "treat" often revolves around the idea of giving medical care or handling someone or something in a certain way, these are the primary meanings to focus on for beginner learners. Therefore, we will provide definitions related to these common uses.

definitions.note: "traité" est utilisé pour décrire un soin ou une manière dont quelque chose a été géré, tandis que "soigné" concerne souvent les soins médicaux.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The patient was treated for his injuries.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le patient a été soigné pour ses blessures.

thoughts: The word "treating" is the present participle of the verb "treat," which means to behave toward someone in a certain way, to give medical care to someone, or to pay for someone as a gift or favor, among other meanings. These are the likely senses that a beginner would encounter. \nFor simplicity, the most common and relevant meaning for English learners would likely involve giving medical care, or more generally, acting a certain way towards someone. However, for the specific form "treating," focusing on providing medical care makes the most sense, as it commonly appears in contexts like "treating a patient."

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The doctor is treating the patient for an infection.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le médecin soigne le patient pour une infection.

thoughts: The word "treatment" as a noun in English commonly refers to the manner in which someone or something is dealt with or managed. It is also frequently used in the medical context to refer to the management and care of a patient to combat a condition or disease. In French, these meanings would translate as "traitement."

definitions.note: Utilisé souvent dans un contexte médical pour désigner une gestion ou un soin.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The treatment he received at the hospital was excellent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le traitement qu'il a reçu à l'hôpital était excellent.

definitions.note: Peut également désigner la manière dont quelqu'un est traité socialement ou professionnellement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Her treatment at work improved after she talked to HR.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Son traitement au travail s'est amélioré après qu'elle ait parlé aux ressources humaines.

thoughts: Given that the word 'treats' is a form of the verb 'treat', I need to ensure that its definitions accurately reflect its usage in sentences. 'Treat' as a verb can mean to act in a certain way towards someone, or it can mean to provide medical care. However, since 'treats' is the third person singular form in the present tense, the example sentence should reflect a simple, everyday context, likely relating to behavior towards someone or something.

definitions.note: Utilisé pour parler de la façon dont quelqu'un se comporte envers une autre personne.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He treats his dog very kindly.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Il traite son chien avec beaucoup de gentillesse.

thoughts: A treaty is a formal agreement between countries. It's important to note this context to accurately translate and explain the term to learners whose native language is French.

definitions.note: Un "traité" est un accord formel entre pays ou gouvernements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The treaty was signed by both nations.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le traité a été signé par les deux nations.

thoughts: The word 'tree' is a common noun referring to a plant with a trunk, branches, and leaves, often grown in gardens, parks, or forests. For beginners in English, it's important to understand the basic meaning of 'tree' as it relates to nature and the environment. Many learners will find the direct translation to French, "arbre," useful along with a simple example sentence that demonstrates its use in context.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: There is a big tree in the garden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Il y a un grand arbre dans le jardin.

thoughts: The word "trees" is the plural form of "tree," a common noun referring to large plants with a single woody stem or trunk. In French, the equivalent is "arbres." Since "trees" is simply the plural form, there are no additional meanings that need to be considered. It's important for learners to see how it is used in context, so I'll provide an example sentence showing how "trees" fits into a natural sentence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The trees in the forest are very tall.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Les arbres de la forêt sont très grands.

thoughts: The word 'tremble' as a verb commonly means to shake involuntarily, typically as a result of anxiety, excitement, or frailty. This is a basic and common meaning that is relevant for beginners to understand. The translation in French would often be "trembler."

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She began to tremble with fear.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle a commencé à trembler de peur.

thoughts: The word "trembled" is the past simple form of the verb "tremble". It means to shake involuntarily, usually because of fear, excitement, or a physical condition. The French translation is most commonly "trembler". An example sentence will help illustrate its use in context.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She trembled with fear when she heard the noise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle tressaillit de peur lorsqu'elle entendit le bruit.

thoughts: The word 'trembling' is the present participle of the verb 'tremble'. For beginner learners, it's vital to focus on the primary meaning of the verb, which is a physical reaction often linked to cold, fear, or excitement. This form can also be used as an adjective to describe something that is shaking or quivering.

definitions.note: Utilisé pour exprimer l'action de trembler à cause du froid, de la peur ou de l'excitation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She is trembling with cold.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle tremble de froid.

thoughts: "Tremendous" is an adjective describing something very large, great, or intense. It is commonly used to emphasize the scale or degree of something, whether it's an amount, size, effort, or shock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The movie was a tremendous success.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le film a connu un succès énorme.

thoughts: The word 'trial' as a noun refers primarily to a legal context, which could mean a process to determine a person's guilt. It can also refer to a test or experiment. This dual definition is essential to include as both meanings are common and useful for beginners.

definitions.note: Utilisé dans un contexte juridique.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The trial will begin tomorrow.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le procès commencera demain.

definitions.note: Utilisé pour un test ou une expérience.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The new drug is going through clinical trials.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le nouveau médicament subit des essais cliniques.

thoughts: The word "tribe" is typically used to refer to a social division in a traditional society, consisting of families or communities linked by social, economic, religious, or blood ties, with a common culture and dialect. In French, this can be translated as "tribu."

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The tribe gathered for the annual ceremony.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: La tribu s'est rassemblée pour la cérémonie annuelle.

thoughts: Le mot 'tribes' est le pluriel du mot 'tribe'. Cela fait référence à des groupes de personnes qui sont souvent unis par la langue, la culture, ou l'ascendance. Il est important de noter que le mot 'tribe' peut avoir différentes connotations culturelles et historiques, alors les utilisateurs doivent être conscients des contextes dans lesquels ils l'utilisent. Le deuxième exemple illustre un autre sens où il peut s'appliquer à des groupes ayant un ensemble d'intérêts ou de caractéristiques communes dans un sens métaphorique, mais ce n'est pas l'usage principal. Puisque c'est le mot 'tribes', c'est surtout au sens propre que les débutants devraient se concentrer.

definitions.note: Dans ce contexte, on parle de groupes sociaux formés généralement sur la base de la famille, de la culture ou de la langue commune.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Many indigenous tribes live in the Amazon rainforest.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: De nombreuses tribus indigènes vivent dans la forêt amazonienne.

definitions.note: Utilisé parfois pour désigner un groupe de personnes ayant des intérêts ou une identité commune, même dans un contexte moderne et métaphorique.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The festival attracted tribes of music lovers from all over the world.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le festival a attiré des communautés de mélomanes du monde entier.

thoughts: The word 'trick' is a noun, which generally means a clever or deceptive act done to achieve a specific purpose. In French, this translates to "truc" or "tour". Beginners should find these definitions straightforward, as they lie in common usage. Example sentences help demonstrate these meanings in context.

definitions.note: Utilisé pour décrire une action habile ou un stratagème pour tromper ou divertir.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He showed us a magic trick with cards.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Il nous a montré un tour de magie avec des cartes.

definitions.note: Peut également être utilisé pour décrire un stratagème destiné à tromper quelqu'un.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She fell for his trick and ended up giving him money.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle a été dupée par son truc et a fini par lui donner de l'argent.

thoughts: The word "tricked" is the past tense of the verb "trick." It commonly means to deceive someone or make them believe something that is not true. In French, the verb "trick" translates to "tromper." For beginner English learners, it is important to highlight the direct translation and provide a relevant example to grasp the usage in context. "Tricked" typically involves a situation where someone has been deceived or fooled, which can be a useful concept to understand in everyday conversations.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He tricked her into believing that he was a famous singer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Il l'a trompée en lui faisant croire qu'il était un chanteur célèbre.

thoughts: The word 'trick' as a noun typically refers to a clever or deceptive act or scheme, often intended to amuse or deceive someone. In the context of beginner English learners, it's important to clarify that 'tricks' is the plural form of 'trick' and generally refers to multiple instances of such acts or schemes. The definition should consider that 'trick' is frequently used in everyday language and is relevant in contexts like games, magic performances, or dishonest actions. In French, 'tricks' could be translated as 'astuces,' 'tours,' or 'pièges,' depending on the context, but for beginners, a simple context like magic tricks may be most illustrative.

definitions.note: Généralement utilisés lors de spectacles de magie ou pour amuser les gens.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: The magician showed some amazing tricks at the show.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Le magicien a montré des tours étonnants pendant le spectacle.

definitions.note: Peut aussi signifier des conseils pratiques ou des méthodes intelligentes pour faire quelque chose.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She shared some clever tricks to save time while cooking.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle a partagé des astuces intelligentes pour gagner du temps en cuisinant.

thoughts: The word "tried" is the past simple form of the verb "try." It is used to describe an action that someone attempted to do in the past. In French, this corresponds to the verb "essayer". It's important to show its use in a simple past context for clarity.

definitions.note: C'est la forme au passé du verbe 'to try'.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She tried to call him yesterday.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle a essayé de l'appeler hier.

thoughts: "Tries" is the third person singular form of the verb "try." It means to make an attempt or effort to do something. This is a word that beginner learners are likely to encounter because it is commonly used in everyday conversation. The main thing to note is that it's used in the present simple tense, typically with subjects like "he," "she," or "it."

definitions.note: Utilisé pour la troisième personne du singulier (ex. il, elle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: She tries to learn English every day.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Elle essaie d'apprendre l'anglais tous les jours.

thoughts: The verb 'trim' is used primarily to refer to the action of cutting or removing parts of something to make it neat, typically referring to hair, plants, or even budgets. This is the most common use of 'trim' that would be relevant to beginner learners.

definitions.note: Utilisé couramment pour se référer à l'action de tailler les cheveux ou les plantes, ou de réduire un budget.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I need to trim the hedge in the garden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Je dois tailler la haie dans le jardin.
